params.body:
## What was fatal

"Gegevens downloaden" in the header of the own-stock list answered 500 on staging:

```
Declaration of App\Exports\defaultExport::collection() must be compatible with
Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\FromCollection::collection(): Illuminate\Support\Enumerable
at app/Exports/defaultExport.php:15
```

`maatwebsite/excel` 4.x declares `collection(): Illuminate\Support\Enumerable` on the
`FromCollection` interface. `App\Exports\defaultExport` still declared `collection()` with no
return type, and PHP refuses such a class at declaration time. The route therefore died before
it read a single vehicle: no amount of data, rights or dealer made a difference, and nothing in
the log pointed at the export itself. It has been broken since the package version went up, so
the feature is dead in production too. Three screens used it: the own-stock download, the dealer
export and the merchant export.

## The fix

The signature now matches the interface, and the property is typed rather than the signature
promising something the property could not hold. The constructor normalises whatever it is given
into an `Enumerable`, so an array caller cannot make the class lie:

- `UserController::downloadExcel` passes a `Collection` of `Collection`s;
- `DealerController::export` and `MerchantController::export` pass a `Collection` of arrays
  (`collect()` of an API resource collection resolves through `jsonSerialize()`).

`headings()` gained one honest branch: an empty export has no columns, where the old code called
`->toArray()` on `null` and turned an empty stock into a second fatal.

## The sweep over app/

Every class in the Composer classmap under `app/` (548 of them) was loaded with the framework
booted and reflected over, which is exactly the instrument for this class of breakage: a method
that no longer satisfies its interface is a load-time error, not a runtime one. Two classes
besides the export cannot be loaded:

- `App\Http\Controllers\Auth\RegisterController` ,  trait `Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\RegistersUsers` not found
- `App\Http\Controllers\Auth\VerificationController` ,  trait `Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\VerifiesEmails` not found

Both are first-day scaffolding from `laravel/ui`, which is not installed. Neither is named by a
route, a view or any other class, so nothing reaches them. Removing or rebuilding them is a
decision rather than a repair, so they are recorded as X-123 and left untouched here.

No other implementation of a `maatwebsite/excel` concern exists: `app/Exports` holds only this
class, and `Excel::download` is called from exactly the three places listed above. There is no
`Excel::store`, no queued export, and no other entry point.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/DownloadExcelTest` does both halves:

- the route is driven as a dealer and the streamed response is read back with PhpSpreadsheet,
  asserting the spreadsheet content type, the `vehicles.xlsx` disposition, and a header row that
  names `chassis_number` and does not name `dealer_id`;
- the class itself is instantiated from a collection of collections, from an array and from an
  empty collection, asserting that `collection()` returns an `Enumerable` and that `headings()`
  holds up. Merely naming the class in a test loads it, which is the assertion that would have
  caught the original fatal on its own.

Both tests fail on `origin/main` (fatal error at class load), and pass with this change.

`php artisan test --filter='Excel|Export|Download|OwnStockList|User|RulesCoverage'`:
**OK (52 tests, 113 assertions)**; with `RulesDocsBuild` added, **OK (54 tests, 117 assertions)**.

## Verified in a running application

Seeded dealer with 2,000 vehicles, logged in as a dealer, followed the "Gegevens downloaden"
link: **200, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`,
`attachment; filename=vehicles.xlsx`, 68,617 bytes, 4.9 s**. The file reads back as
**2,001 rows by 116 columns** (header plus 2,000 vehicles), with the coupled fields as names
(`dealer`, `model`, `fuel_type`, ...) and the internal ids absent, as the rule says.

## Open point, not fixed here: the download is built entirely in memory

`downloadExcel` loads every vehicle of the dealer, converts each one to an array, resolves eleven
relations per vehicle and hands the whole set to the writer. Measured on this machine, on the
same route:

| vehicles | seconds | peak memory above baseline | bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2,000 | 4.7 | 96 MB | 68,617 |
| 8,000 | 18.1 | 313 MB | 251,863 |

That is roughly 40 KB and 2.3 ms per vehicle, and it scales linearly. A dealer the size of
De Backer is already in the thousands, so a 256 MB `memory_limit` is reached somewhere around
5,000 vehicles and a 30 s execution limit somewhere around 13,000, a limit that will be hit
long before anyone calls the feature slow, and it will look exactly like the 500 this PR just
fixed. Recorded as an open point; chunking the query and writing row by row (or queueing the
export) is the repair, and it belongs in its own change.

## Docs

- R P1-1.12 now says what the download actually is (an xlsx named `vehicles.xlsx`, with a header
  row, coupled fields as names, internal ids absent, scoped to the own dealer), so that the rule
  is testable rather than a sentence.
- X-122 records the defect; X-123 records the two unloadable auth controllers.

`docs/bedrijfsregels.html` and `docs/bedrijfsregels/92-testdekking-tabel.md` are generated and
gitignored; they were not regenerated.
